after.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(y)=2{y}^{2}-8y+26.$

Next, we solve $f(y)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =0 \\ 2{y}^{2}-8y+26 & =0 \\ {y}^{2}-4y+13 & =0 \\ ({y}^{2}-2\cdot 2\cdot y+{2}^{2})-{2}^{2}+13 & =0 \\ (y-2)^{2}-4+13 & =0 \\ (y-2)^{2}+9 & =0 \\ (y-2)^{2} & =-9 \\ (y-2)^{2} & =9{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (y-2)^{2} & ={(3\text{i})}^{2} \\ y-2 & =\pm 3\text{i} \\ y & =2\pm 3\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since our quadratic equation has roots ${y}_{1}=2+3\text{i}$ and ${y}_{2}=2-3\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=2,$ the expression $2{y}^{2}-8y+26$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-8y+26 & =a(y-{y}_{1})(y-{y}_{2}) \\  & =2(y-(2+3\text{i}))(y-(2-3\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(y)$ has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=3,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=3.$ Find $P(y).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=3,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=3,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(y-{y}_{1})^{2} & =3{(y-3)}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3{(y-3)}^{2} & =3({y}^{2}-6y+9) \\  & =3{y}^{2}-18y+27.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(y)=3{y}^{2}-18y+27.$

after.problem: Which of the following is a factor of ${u}^{2}-4u+40?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we let $f(u)={u}^{2}-4u+40.$

Next, we solve $f(u)=0$ by completing the square, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(u) & =0 \\ {u}^{2}-4u+40 & =0 \\ ({u}^{2}-2\cdot 2\cdot u+{2}^{2})-{2}^{2}+40 & =0 \\ (u-2)^{2}-4+40 & =0 \\ (u-2)^{2}+36 & =0 \\ (u-2)^{2} & =-36 \\ (u-2)^{2} & =36{\text{i}}^{2} \\ (u-2)^{2} & =(6\text{i})^{2} \\ u-2 & =\pm 6\text{i} \\ u & =2\pm 6\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Since our quadratic equation has roots ${u}_{1}=2+6\text{i}$ and ${u}_{2}=2-6\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1,$ the expression ${u}^{2}-4u+40$ can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{u}^{2}-4u+40 & =a(u-{u}_{1})(u-{u}_{2}) \\  & =(u-(2+6\text{i}))(u-(2-6\text{i})).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, among the given options, only $u-(2-6\text{i})$ is a factor of ${u}^{2}-4u+40.$

after.problem: The quadratic polynomial $f(v)$ has real coefficients, has roots ${v}_{1}=3+4\text{i}$ and ${v}_{2}=3-4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $2.$ Find $f(v).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${v}_{1}=3+4\text{i}$ and ${v}_{2}=3-4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(v-{v}_{1})(v-{v}_{2}) & =2(v-(3+4\text{i}))(v-(3-4\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(v-(3+4\text{i}))(v-(3-4\text{i})) & =2({v}^{2}-(3+4\text{i})v-(3-4\text{i})v+(3+4\text{i})(3-4\text{i})) \\  & =2({v}^{2}-(3+4\text{i}+3-4\text{i})v+({3}^{2}-{4}^{2}{\text{i}}^{2})) \\  & =2({v}^{2}-6v+(9+16)) \\  & =2{v}^{2}-12v+50.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(v)=2{v}^{2}-12v+50.$

$$

\begin{aligned}(-2){(y-7)}^{2} & =(-2)({y}^{2}-14y+49) \\  & =-2{y}^{2}+28y-98.\end{aligned}
$$
